 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Shashank Shekhar Jha, Adv.
 For the Respondent/s : Mrs. Nutan Sahay, Aag 12
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajiv Roy
 Oral Order
2 03-02-2026 Heard Mr. Shashank Shekhar Jha, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mrs. Nutan Sahay for the State.

2. The present application has been preferred for the following relief(s):
(i) Issuance of a writ/direction including a order of writ in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents to Patna High Court CWJC No.24683 of 2018(2)
dt.03-02-2026 release the compensation amount of the acquired land according to market value after rectification of type of land as 'residential' by the Govt. of Bihar at Village- Gandaul, Than No.-72, Anchal Mahishi, District- Saharsa, which is acquired for construction of Link road with R.C.C. Bridge as enhancement breath of of the existing Road (State Highway) No. 17.
(ii) Issuance a direction also to of follow all the procedure Acquisition in accordance with RFCTLARR- Act-2013 (Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Naresh Mohan Choudhary And Ors vs The State Of Bihar And Ors on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110274219/
2 Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act-2013)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and classify the type of land as 'Residential instead of 'Dhanber-2. or Veeth-2'.
(iii) Any other relief/reliefs may be granted to petitioners as he is found entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case for the ends of Justice.
3. The matter relates to Land Acquisition Case No. 04 of 2013-14 for construction of Link road with R.C.C. Bridge over Kosi river.
The petitioners' claim is that their lands also were part of the compensation.

4. It is to be noted that altogether 44 petitioners have approached this Court in single writ petition and in that background, the claim put forward by them have to be Patna High Court CWJC No.24683 of 2018(2) dt.03-02-2026 adjudicated individually.
The document also shows that notices were issued to them individually, though they chose to submit objection by way of representation of altogether 79 persons.

5. Learned State Counsel submits that notices were issued, it is not the further claim of the petitioner that award has not been prepared and if they have not provided documents/payment not taken, they have to move before appropriate authority challenging the award.

6. This Court is also of the view that the Government by way of advertisement took steps for the acquisition of the land, petitioners were individually noticed, they should have moved forward along with their separate documents to satisfy the authority so that appropriate compensation is extended to them.
In case, they have any objection, would have moved before appropriate authority.
8. It goes without saying that if such individual petitions come, the same has to be taken to its logical conclusion.
9. The writ petition is disposed of with aforesaid observations.

(Rajiv Roy, J) Vijay Singh/-
